header: Date: 2026-03-25 14:00 PT | Duration: ~38m | Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Carlos Ruiz (Redwood SE), Ellen Zhou (CSM), Tom Everett (Aurora Eng Lead), Priya Shah (Product), Daniel Kim (Infra), Speaker 1 (QA)
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on rollout planning for Aurora's pilot to production. Key topics: canary strategy (traffic split and metric gates), A/B test variant for model quantization, monitoring/alerting and runbooks, cutover weekend logistics, security sign-offs (SOC2 and SSO), and next steps for synthetic load testing and runbook delivery.
topics: A/B tests: quantized vs fp16 model variant
Monitoring: p95 latency, error rate, model quality regression checks
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: All right everyone, thanks for joining. we're on for the 30 minute weekly, we have about 38 minutes on the calendar, i added a little extra for the rollout discussion. um Tom, Priya, Daniel, thanks for making time.
[00:12] Tom Everett: Yep, thanks Maya. quick heads-up, we have a stakeholder call right after but should be fine.
[00:18] Carlos Ruiz: hi team, Carlos from Redwood SE. today i'd like to run through the canary approach, monitoring gates, and the runbook we'll ask you to exercise during canary. also quick status on the perf tests we ran last week.
[00:32] Priya Shah: quick question — is this going to include the A/B we talked about? the quantized model variant vs the fp16?
[00:39] Carlos Ruiz: yes, we recommend a small A/B during canary: 90/10 baseline (fp16) vs quantized variant to validate quality metrics and cost delta.
[00:47] Speaker 1: there's some background noise — sorry.
[00:50] Maya Patel: no worries, speaker 1. i'll also cover the commercial bits later — specifically dedicated burst pricing for the first month of go-live and guardrails.
[00:58] Daniel Kim: on infra side, we validated VPC peering last week but want to test firewall stateful rules during canary. i will need the exact IP ranges.
[01:07] Carlos Ruiz: i'll include the IP ranges in the runbook doc. note that we also support TLS mutual for traffic to private deployment if you want to exercise that.
[01:16] Tom Everett: perfect. can we step through the canary plan now? like minute-by-minute or more high-level?
[01:21] Carlos Ruiz: high-level with explicit gating is usually better — too much minute-by-minute gets noisy. here's the proposed flow:
[01:29] - Day 0: dry run — smoke tests, run synthetic load at 10% of expected peak.
[01:35] - Day 1: Canary kickoff (weekday low-traffic window) — route 2% production traffic to canary for 2 hours.
[01:43] - Gate 1: p95 latency < 250ms and error rate < 0.5% sustained over 15min.
[01:49] - If pass, increase to 10% for 4 hours with additional model quality checks (QA prompt set).
[01:57] - Gate 2: model quality delta (BLEU-ish/semantic score) less than agreed threshold and no user-facing errors.
[02:05] - If pass, ramp to 50% during off-peak night window, then full cutover next day or weekend based on success.
[02:12] Priya Shah: when you say model quality checks, do you have an automated eval harness or will that be manual?
[02:18] Carlos Ruiz: Redwood can run the automated eval harness — we'll score the sample prompt-set you provided last week. there's a brief manual review step by your QA team for edge cases.
[02:27] Tom Everett: what's the sampling size for the prompt set? is it 500 prompts or smaller?
[02:31] Carlos Ruiz: we recommend 300–500 depending on variance; for this pilot we suggested 350.
[02:36] Speaker 1: (muffled) 350 sounds good.
[02:40] Maya Patel: on budget/commercials: if you hit the pilot overage we talked about a 20% discounted overage rate for the first 30 days — i'll send the updated pricing in email.
[02:50] Tom Everett: great, thanks.
[02:52] Carlos Ruiz: quick perf note from last week's bench: under synthetic conditions the baseline fp16 at your typical seq len distribution had p95 of 210ms, quantized variant had p95 of 230ms but cost per token down ~32%. these are with our batching and KV cache turned on — though we saw cache hit rate vary across endpoints.
[03:14] Daniel Kim: did you see any tail spikes or OOMs on the quantized path?
[03:18] Carlos Ruiz: tail spikes were minimal once we tuned batch size; no OOMs. we did find one path where KV cache warmed slower — looked like a prefix mismatch in a few user sessions. we flagged it and updated cache keying.
[03:30] Priya Shah: is the KV cache the same as K-V cash in the docs? (laughs)
[03:34] Carlos Ruiz: (laughs) sometimes transcription spells it K-V cash. it's KV cache, key-value cache. important for latency and cost.
[03:40] Maya Patel: moving on to monitoring and alerts — Carlos, what's the minimum set you recommend for canary?
[03:46] Carlos Ruiz: core gates: p95 latency, overall error rate, upstream 5xx ratio, model quality regression metric from eval harness, token cost per minute. plus functional checks for top-10 user flows. alerting: PagerDuty for sev1, slack channel for sev2, and an email summary every 30 minutes during ramp.
[04:05] Tom Everett: who owns the runbooks on our side? we'll likely want to map our on-call to your incident playbook.
[04:11] Ellen Zhou: Redwood provides the runbook and we ask the customer to map their on-call roles into it — we can include the mapping template.
[04:19] Daniel Kim: we need the incident playbook to include rollback steps: immediate traffic cut, redirect to hosted fallback, and KMS key revocation steps?
[04:28] Carlos Ruiz: yes, we'll have a rollback play with clear steps: 1) shift traffic back to hosted API (URL + keys in vault), 2) scale up a known-good model node pool if needed, 3) engage infra. KMS revocation we treat carefully — that would be a last resort. we'll document which keys to rotate vs revoke.
[04:45] Speaker 1: transcription: sam-el (SAML) was requested for SSO — is that in place?
[04:50] Maya Patel: we have SAML SSO configured for the console; for the private plane (private control plane) we'll guide you on SAML metadata and SP-initiated flow. we'll also provide SOC 2 documentation and the audit log export format.
[05:05] Priya Shah: how long to get SOC 2 artifacts? we need them for our procurement checklist.
[05:09] Maya Patel: i'll attach the pack in email today — it's the standard SOC 2 Type II with the mapping sheet. expect a 24–48 hour turnaround for the detailed pack.
[05:17] Tom Everett: ok. back to canary windows — you suggested a weekday low-traffic window first, then weekend cutover. our preference is weekend midnight-4am — fewer users. any reason not to do that?
[05:29] Carlos Ruiz: weekend is fine — advantage is more room for full ramp if needed. only caveat: make sure your on-call is staffed; also the eval manual review might be slower on weekend.
[05:40] Priya Shah: can we run the A/B variant only on 5% of traffic instead of 10%? we want to be more conservative on quality.
[05:46] Carlos Ruiz: yes, start at 2–5% is fine. the tradeoff is slower statistical confidence, but given your prompts and low variance we've seen 5% give meaningful signal.
[05:58] Tom Everett: what about fallback — you mentioned hosted fallback. will that be the Redwood hosted API or our old model?
[06:05] Carlos Ruiz: hosted Redwood API is the fastest fallback path we operate. we can also configure a route to your legacy model if you prefer; that'll need a connector and auth mapping.
[06:15] Daniel Kim: for the canary we'll want synthetic traffic that includes some burst patterns to exercise batching. can you generate that?
[06:22] Carlos Ruiz: yes, we'll run a synthetic that mirrors your real-time distribution — bursts + steady-state. we'll also run a TTL test to ensure cache warms in the expected timeframe.
[06:33] Speaker 1: (inaudible) caching TTLs?
[06:35] Carlos Ruiz: TTL on the prefix cache is configurable; we recommend 24h for your workload but during canary we can shorten to 1h to observe warming behavior.
[06:44] Maya Patel: quick note on rollback and data retention — Aurora asked about logs and audit retention in the private deployment.
[06:51] Priya Shah: yes, we need 12 months of audit logs and ability to search by token id.
[06:56] Ellen Zhou: Redwood's private deployment supports configurable retention; 12 months is supported, and audit export is S3-compatible. we'll include the exact schema in the security pack.
[07:07] Tom Everett: great. who will be primary contact during cutover?
[07:10] Maya Patel: Maya and Carlos will be primary for product and infra respectively, and Ellen will run comms. on your side, Tom and Daniel. we'll include names in the runbook.
[07:20] Daniel Kim: any special metrics we should monitor for the quantized model other than latency and errors?
[07:25] Carlos Ruiz: watch token-efficiency and semantic quality delta. also monitor GPU utilization if you're on Dedicated; quantized runs lower utilization but sometimes shows higher variance under burst.
[07:38] Priya Shah: about Dedicated vs Hosted — do we need Dedicated for go-live?
[07:42] Maya Patel: recommended if you need strict isolation, predictable throughput, or want to avoid noisy-neighbor bursts. Hosted is usually OK for most customers at scale, but Dedicated gives you the SLA and reserved capacity. for the pilot we planned a dedicated pool with burst to hosted as fallback.
[08:00] Tom Everett: cost delta to move to Dedicated? ballpark?
[08:03] Maya Patel: i'll send the committed capacity quote but ballpark it's higher fixed cost with lower per-token variable. we included that in the term sheet; i'll re-share.
[08:12] Speaker 1: (background) Are we good on encryption at rest?
[08:16] Ellen Zhou: yes, encryption at rest with KMS is standard; we support customer-managed keys in private deployment. we'll document key rotation recommendations.
[08:26] Carlos Ruiz: another operational note — for the canary we recommend a feature flag client-side to isolate users exposed to the new model. that allows quick rollback without infra changes.
[08:39] Priya Shah: do we have a timeframe for running the synthetic load?
[08:43] Carlos Ruiz: we can run it next Tuesday (2026-03-31) and share results by end of day.
[08:49] Tom Everett: Tuesday works. Daniel, does that fit your infra schedule?
[08:52] Daniel Kim: yep, we can carve out a maintenance window.
[08:55] Maya Patel: excellent. i want to read out the runbook sections we'll deliver: pre-checks, traffic gating, metric thresholds, manual QA checklist, rollback steps, infra checklist (IP ranges, firewall), and comms plan.
[09:08] Carlos Ruiz: plus links to dashboards: p95 latency, error rate, model-quality score, token cost chart, and a canary summary. we'll include sample alert definitions.
[09:18] Speaker 1: any issues with alerts firing too often?
[09:22] Carlos Ruiz: we tune thresholds based on baseline traffic; during canary we add a 15min suppress window to avoid noisy flapping, then tighten.
[09:30] Priya Shah: i want to confirm the manual QA step — is that a human reviewing N examples flagged by the harness or a random sample?
[09:37] Carlos Ruiz: both. harness flags anomalies; then QA does a stratified random sample including flagged cases.
[09:43] Tom Everett: what if the quality delta is slightly above threshold but latency and error gates pass — do we abort?
[09:50] Maya Patel: that's a judgement call — for minor deltas we may continue with narrower exposure while product reviews examples. for major regressions abort and rollback. we'll put decision criteria in runbook.
[09:59] Daniel Kim: do you have an SLA on rollback time? like TTR target?
[10:03] Ellen Zhou: target rollback within 15 minutes for traffic cut; full mitigation depends on root cause but 2 hours is our emergency target to restore normal function.
[10:12] Priya Shah: can you circulate a sample post-mortem template?
[10:15] Ellen Zhou: yes, we'll include PM template in the runbook pack.
[10:20] Carlos Ruiz: one more perf remark — we tracked p95 by route; a couple of edge routes were higher due to long prompt lengths. trimming prompts or forcing shorter max tokens for those routes reduced p95 by ~40ms.
[10:33] Tom Everett: okay good to know. we'll identify top 5 heavy routes and consider limits.
[10:38] Maya Patel: any concerns on compliance? procurement usually asks for encryption, SOC, SSO, and incident response. we covered SOC and SAML, anything else?
[10:48] Priya Shah: retention / e-discovery question — can audit logs be exported to our SIEM?
[10:52] Ellen Zhou: yes S3 export and we can push via connector to common SIEMs; we'll include example parsers.
[10:59] Speaker 1: (inaudible)
[11:02] Carlos Ruiz: quick timeline recap: synthetic test 2026-03-31, runbook by 2026-03-27, confirm cutover window by 2026-03-30, proposed cutover weekend 2026-04-10.
[11:15] Tom Everett: 2026-04-10 looks OK for us, pending a final yes after synthetic results.
[11:20] Maya Patel: good. final admin — i'll send meeting notes and the runbook link after this call. any other blockers?
[11:27] Daniel Kim: just the IP ranges and the firewall rules doc for the peering test.
[11:32] Carlos Ruiz: i'll attach that.
[11:34] Priya Shah: thanks all.
[11:36] Maya Patel: thanks everyone. Ellen will set the follow-up for post-canary review.
[11:41] (call ends)
